annotations.label: bisection method
annotations.text: The bisection method, in particular, is a classic, derivative-free algorithm for finding roots of continuous functions.
annotations.notes: Body definition introducing the bisection method as a derivative-free root-finding algorithm.

annotations.label: Bolzano's Theorem
annotations.text: Bolzano's Theorem states that a real-valued function f, continuous on a closed interval [a, b] ⊆ R, and such that f(a) and f(b) have opposite signs, has a root inside the open interval (a, b).
annotations.notes: Explicit statement/definition of Bolzano's Theorem in the body.

annotations.label: fixed-point method
annotations.text: the FPM approximates fixed points of its input functions. These are points r such that f(r) = r... The fixed-point method starts from an initial guess x0 and repeatedly applies f: xn+1 = f(xn).
annotations.notes: Body definition of the fixed-point method (FPM).

annotations.label: contractive set
annotations.text: if there is a constant c such that |g(x) − g(y)| ≤ c |x − y| and 0 < c < 1, for x, y ∈ S, then the function g is c-contractive on S, or equivalently, S is a contractive set for g.
annotations.notes: Definition of c-contractive function and contractive set.

annotations.label: verification condition generation
annotations.text: Hoare logic and verification condition generation (VCG) for algorithms operating over the real numbers, including total correctness.
annotations.notes: Introduces VCG as the verification mechanism used by the framework.

annotations.label: Isabelle/ITrees
annotations.text: Our verification approach is based on the Isabelle/ITrees framework... The programs are assigned a formal semantics in terms of Interaction Trees (ITrees), which unify denotational and operational semantics for programs.
annotations.notes: Definition/introduction of the Isabelle/ITrees framework underlying the work.

annotations.label: Interaction Trees
annotations.text: Interaction Trees (ITrees), which unify denotational and operational semantics for programs. In particular, ITrees, as coinductively defined data structures, are fundamentally executable in nature
annotations.notes: Defines Interaction Trees as coinductive data structures unifying denotational/operational semantics.

annotations.label: Newton's Method
annotations.text: Newton's Method, a special case of the Fixed-Point Method with quadratic convergence. This yields the fixed-point iteration xk+1 = g(xk), g(x) = x − f(x)/f'(x) = (1/2)(x + 3/x).
annotations.notes: Body characterisation of Newton's Method as a special case of FPM.

annotations.label: Taylor's theorem (Peano form)
annotations.text: higher-order derivatives and Taylor's theorem in Peano form
annotations.notes: Key contributed result; defined/used throughout Sections 5–6.
